Messages.Author: Guy Keen
Messages.Body:
I play a heavy bleed deck that starts out short on obfuscate skill, so
Cloak of the Gathering is a handy card, as I understand it.

But I'm not sure if I'm reading the superior skill correctly. That is:

If I have an acting vamp with superior obfuscate (presumably taking
any action), it can use CotG as a modifier to give +1 stealth to
another vamp, even one belonging to another Methuselah.

If this is correct, it raises a few questions in my mind:

1. Does the recipient vampire have to be ready? (It would seem not)
2. For how long does the recipient gain the +1 stealth? (Anything
longer than the current turn would be excessive I think)
3. Does it matter whether or not the acting vampire is tapped? (Again
it would seem not)
4. Can 1 vampire play more than 1 CotG per action? (It would seem so)

So, if vamp1 performs an action and is tapped, and vamp2 (with superior
Obfuscate) modifies its action with 1 or more CotG, then vamp1 could
conceivably play a Freak Drive and prepare another action at +1
or more stealth.

I love the sound of this, so I'd be interested in any serious feedback on my
interpretations.

***Guy***

Messages.Author: Joseph Cochran
Messages.Body:
In article <321896...@hceltd.demon.co.uk>,

Guy Keen <G...@hceltd.demon.co.uk> wrote:
>But I'm not sure if I'm reading the superior skill correctly. That is:
>
> If I have an acting vamp with superior obfuscate (presumably taking
> any action), it can use CotG as a modifier to give +1 stealth to
> another vamp, even one belonging to another Methuselah.

No, that's not it. It's a very poorly worded card. Here's how
it works:

It is usable by a minion other than the acting minion. That
other minion gives +1 stealth to the acting minion. It is only usable
on your turn.

So for example: Rake calls a vote. Basilia on a sport bike
tries to block. Sheldon, one of Rake's friends, lends Rake a little
stealth. Basilia gets superior Cat's Guidance. Agrippina lends Rake a
little more stealth. The vote gets called.

Note a key advantage to Cloak that works out in the above
example: Since it is not played by the acting minion, but is instead
played by other minions, it can be used more than once during the same
action.

Messages.Author: L. Scott Johnson
Messages.Body:
G...@hceltd.demon.co.uk (Guy Keen) writes:





A. CtG is an Action modifier and can only modify the stealth of the Acting
Vampire. Since other methuselah's minions are not acting (Madness.Net
notwithstanding), you can't modify their stealth.

B. You can't play action modifiers that give stealth nor reaction cards
that give intercept unless you need them. You can take actions that
do so any time (hey, they're actions, right?).
(Little rulebook, p.28 para 2&3.)

CtG is an action modifier, so it can't be played unless you need the stealth.

Messages.Author: Shane Hamish William Travis
Messages.Body:
Guy Keen (G...@hceltd.demon.co.uk) wrote:

: There is such a thing as this - that's how Psychic Projection (All

: minions have +1 intercept until your next untap phase) and Psychic Veil
: (+1 stealth to all vampires'/minions' actions this turn) work. One
: vampire takes the action, and if it's successful, the other vampires
: benefit accordingly. I'm suggesting that CotG apples in a similar fashion.

This is an example of the card text overriding the basic rules, as hapens
often in almost all CCGs.

Psychic projection _has_ to say "...until your next untap phase." because
if it didn't it would be a pretty useless card. The rulebook says:

"Increased stealth and intercept return to normal after the action is
resolved." (13.3.2 - last sentence before examples.)

Note - it does not say "...increased stealth/intercept _of the acting and
blocking minions_ ...", thus _all_ increased stealth/intercept returns to
normal. It has to, or someone could try this trick:

A: I bleed at +1 stealth
B: I use enhanced sensed on V1 to get +1 intercept and block.
A: I increase stealth to +2
B: I use Sup. Enhanced Senses on V2 to get +2 intercept and block.
A: I increase stealth to +3.
B: I declare V3 as a new blocker, and use cards to give him +3 intercept.
A: Blocked.

[Combat]

A: Cool. Now since increased Stealth/intercept only returns to normal for
the blocker and acting vamp, I now have V1 with +1 intercept and V2 with
+2 intercept. That was fun.... Do somthing - I want to block it...

(remember: V1 and V2 are _not_ blockers in the game sense of the word,
since they were unsuccessful in their blocks.)

If you wanna play this way as a house rule, more power to ya - just be
sure that everyone knows that it _is_ a house rule.

Messages.Body:
Guy Keen (G...@hceltd.demon.co.uk) wrote:
: I play a heavy bleed deck that starts out short on obfuscate skill, so

: 1. Does the recipient vampire have to be ready? (It would seem not)

Yes, the recipient should be ready. Why? Becasue you are stealthing an
action that the recipient is making. It would be pointless to stealth
a vampire that cna't do anything on this turn.
: 2. For how long does the recipient gain the +1 stealth? (Anything

: longer than the current turn would be excessive I think)

Well, the most (not all) stealth and intercept cards work, is that the
vampire gains stealth for the action that it is performing. So, if you
performing an action using that stealth, it's gone once you're
done. You can't save steralth, except by holding the card in your hand
til a later time...(=
: 3. Does it matter whether or not the acting vampire is tapped? (Again
: it would seem not)
I think it matters...ok, you've got atpaped vamp...he can't do
anything...what happens? He sits there twiddling his thumbs..but he's
really stealthy at it...utterly useless...
: 4. Can 1 vampire play more than 1 CotG per action? (It would seem so)
No, to use the CotG you have to tap the vampire...once tapped it can't
play another one. Get another vamp with obfuscate to do it.

Messages.Author: Purple Kitty
Messages.Body:
Guy Keen (G...@hceltd.demon.co.uk) wrote:
: I play a heavy bleed deck that starts out short on obfuscate skill, so

: Cloak of the Gathering is a handy card, as I understand it.

: But I'm not sure if I'm reading the superior skill correctly. That is:

: If I have an acting vamp with superior obfuscate (presumably taking
: any action), it can use CotG as a modifier to give +1 stealth to
: another vamp, even one belonging to another Methuselah.

True...unless it says "...a minion you control", you can give it to
anyone. (I don't have the card on hand right now). Note that it's any
MINION, not any vampire. Big difference when using allies.

: If this is correct, it raises a few questions in my mind:

: 1. Does the recipient vampire have to be ready? (It would seem not)

Yes, obviously! Because a vampire in torpor (or uncontrolled) cannot take
an action! What you need to grok here is that CotG is an ACTION MODIFIER,
that modifies the other minion's current action.

: 2. For how long does the recipient gain the +1 stealth? (Anything

: longer than the current turn would be excessive I think)

Again, it is an ACTION MODIFIER, so it only applies to the action it's
being used for.

: 3. Does it matter whether or not the acting vampire is tapped? (Again
: it would seem not)

Because a tapped vampire cannot take an action, you cannot use CtG to
give a tapped vampire stealth.

: 4. Can 1 vampire play more than 1 CotG per action? (It would seem so)

Each minion may only play one action modifier per action (read the small
book). But you COULD have three different vamps with Sup. Obfuscate use
CtG on one vamp for his current action, giving him +3 stealth.

: So, if vamp1 performs an action and is tapped, and vamp2 (with superior

: Obfuscate) modifies its action with 1 or more CotG, then vamp1 could
: conceivably play a Freak Drive and prepare another action at +1
: or more stealth.

Nope.

If you want an example or something to help understand better, let me know.

The vampire needs to be untapped to take the action to be stealthed, but
need not be "ready", which means being controlled yet out of torpor.
There are a few actions possible in torpor.

>: 3. Does it matter whether or not the acting vampire is tapped? (Again
>: it would seem not)

>anything...what happens? He sits there twiddling his thumbs..but he's

Worse than that - since he's untapped, he can't take an action, so there
is no action to modify. CotG isn't merely useless, it can't be played.

>[...]

Note that there is a DTR somewhere that says that this phrase
should read that *minions* cannot repeat action modifiers. The phrase
in 7.2.2 is correct and this one is wrong. Players are perfectly free
to use multiples of action modifiers provided that they can get multiple
minions working in the same action.

No, this is _not true of most cards:

14. Summary of the Course of an Action
[...]
4. ... Players cannot play the same action modifier card more than once
per action.

This means that I cannot use three superior Voter Captivations to gain 6
blood avter a successful vote, I can't use two Srocn of Adonis to make
everyone lose 2 pool if they vote against me, I can't use 4 Bonding to
end up with a +4 Bleed at +4 stealth.

The restrictions on Bonding/Conditioning/Threats FURTHER restrict this
rule by saying that if you use one of these cards, not only cannot use
another _of that same card_, but you cannot use another card _from that
group_ either; without that card text there would be nothing to stop you
from using all three to get (at most) a +6 bleed at +1 stealth. Just a
_little_ abusive... :-)

: I think the purpose of CtG is to give stealth to your acting vampire
: that does not have enough stealth. This is done by a vampire
: that has superior obfuscate. It all happens when it is your turn. I
: don't have the card with me but didn't it say that the vampire playing
: CtG is tapped?

Action modifiers do not tap the minion playing them. The original poster
had the right idea as to the strength of this card.

Messages.Author: Joseph Cochran
Messages.Body:
In article <marko.7...@snakemail.hut.fi>,
Marko Puumalainen <ma...@beta.hut.fi> wrote:
>If you mean that you can use the same card twice I think you're
>wrong. Once you use a card you place it in your ash heap and cannot
>use it again.

Most definitely.

>If you mean that you can use more than one CtG card per action, it is
>true with most other action modifiers, too. The exceptions are
>mentioned in the cards (Threats, Bonding, Conditioning).

Most definitely not. From the Rules, section 7.2.2 "Minion
Cards," paragraph on Action modifier cards: "The same action modifier
card type cannot be used twice by a minion during the same action." The
B/C/T says that if you use of of those types, you can't use others of
those types, which is a further restriction to the above rule.

>I think the purpose of CtG is to give stealth to your acting vampire
>that does not have enough stealth. This is done by a vampire
>that has superior obfuscate. It all happens when it is your turn. I
>don't have the card with me but didn't it say that the vampire playing
>CtG is tapped?

Yes, it does give stealth to someone who doesn't have enough.
Yes, it does happen during your turn. If you happen to have 2 minions
other than the acting minion who have Sup. Obfs. then, they can each
loan the acting minion a stealth.
Oh, and the card says "does not tap the playing vampire." RTFC.
